routeSelection.route: Molecular Life Sciences, ordinary route with neutral first-listed 18-EC ML1 selection
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English-taught Molecular Life Sciences bachelor, not one optional year-three thematic menu or an educational minor. The adopted EER specifies one shared core and a flexible differentiation phase. The first three ML1 items are neutral first-listed choices solely to instantiate the 18-EC minimum; the other 39 EC remains accurately represented as restricted selection.

alternatives.label: Molecular, cellular & biomedical life sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, disease, laboratory work, neuroscience and quantitative analysis form the visible spine; the label does not claim UCR offers the target’s chemistry sequence.
alternatives.concept: Study molecular and cellular life through biochemistry, physiology, genetics, immunity, disease, laboratory work, neurobiology and quantitative analysis. This is the strongest related-fields response to Molecular Life Sciences; it does not reproduce Radboud’s organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry or its synthesis and specialist laboratory sequence.
progression: Life-science, brain-and-behaviour, programming, mathematics, statistics and data foundations precede molecular biology, physiology, laboratory work, genetics, disease, immunity, pharmacology and advanced analysis. All formal prerequisites and exact planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, genetics and biomolecular mechanisms
Human biology, biomedical research, disease and medical applications
Programming, statistics, imaging and structural analysis for molecular research
Neurobiology, perception, cognition and brain development
Scientific reasoning and ethics in molecular and biomedical inquiry
questions: How do molecular and cellular processes produce biological function, disease and treatment possibilities?
How can molecular and biomedical questions be investigated experimentally and quantitatively?
How do molecular and cellular mechanisms support brain function, perception and development?

candidates.label: Neurobiology, brain function & biological health
candidates.assessment: Official neurobiology is a genuine optional direction, but the proposed second UCR route devotes major weight to philosophy of mind,abnormal/health/lifespanpsychology andpsycholinguistics,omits molecular lab and does not provide molecular neurobiology,neurodevelopment or translationalresearch. Replacing those with available molecular/data/labcourses collapses toward main. No distinct feasible MLSresponse retained.

candidates.label: Functional genomics & human biology
candidates.assessment: The closest programme already centres molecular-cell biology, genetics, immunity, human physiology and disease. The UCR catalogue does not support a genuinely different functional-genomics curriculum; substitutions would be cosmetic rather than a new organising direction.

candidates.label: Chemistry of life & medicinal chemistry
candidates.assessment: UCR offers Biochemistry, Pharmacology and one broad Life Science Laboratory, but no sequence in analytical, organic, inorganic or physical chemistry, synthesis, spectroscopy, crystallography or medicinal chemistry. A complete chemistry-led alternative would require unrelated filler and would misstate the defining curriculum.

candidates.label: Specialist microscopy and molecular imaging
candidates.assessment: UCRbasicneurobiologymicroscopyandimageprocessingaregenuine,butdonotconstitute a distinct specialist molecular imaging/structure programme or reproduce targetfacilities.

blocks: Molecular and biomedical coverage with explicit specialist gaps
Python programming and computational problem solving contribute to the programming part; the target also requires statistics and its molecular context.
Calculus and differential-equation techniques contribute to mathematical foundations; this single UCR course does not replicate the target’s complete 9 EC mathematics.
Biomolecules,metabolism and biochemical mechanisms provide substantive biochemical coverage; this does not supply the separate chemistry sequence.
Gene expression,genomes,cell dynamics and molecular research methods provide related molecular-cell coverage,with differences in depth and experimental specialisation.
Protein and DNA laboratory techniques,ELISA,electrophoresis and bacterial work provide genuine introductory biochemical laboratory coverage; not the target’s whole multi-lab sequence.
Innate/adaptive immunity,lymphocyte receptors and host-pathogen interactions provide related immunology coverage; specialist scope differs.

notes.text: Radboud Molecular Life Sciences integrates molecular biology with sustained organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, synthesis and several specialist laboratories. UCR can study molecular, cellular, biomedical and neurobiological questions through biology, biochemistry, data and one broad life-science laboratory, but these programmes are related-fields responses rather than reproductions of the full molecular-science curriculum.

audience.programmeDescription: Molecular Life Sciences at Radboud combines molecular biology and medical science with a substantial foundation in chemistry, physics and mathematics. Students study molecular processes in health and disease through theory, computational work and laboratory research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR programme develops molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, genetics, immunity, pharmacology and disease mechanisms, supported by laboratory work and quantitative methods. It offers a related biomedical route. It does not reproduce Radboud’s organic, inorganic, analytical and physical chemistry, synthesis, spectroscopy, crystallography, specialist laboratory sequence or required research internship.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary Molecular Life Sciences route; one permitted 18 EC elective selection
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC framework consists of 105 EC required courses, 57 EC restricted differentiation study, a 12 EC research internship and 6 EC open electives. The three displayed 6 EC ML1 courses illustrate the required 18 EC selection. The other 39 EC must meet programme rules and is not unrestricted free choice. Academic skills, language assessment and writing requirements are integrated as specified; the first-year skills component and language assessment add no credits.

componentNotes.later-required-03: The first-year skills component carries no credits and includes writing assignments, a progress test, reflection and mandatory mentor activities. Final skills credits require portfolio completion, mentor meetings and twelve documented colloquia or similar activities across years two and three.
componentNotes.later-required-10: Choose one permitted 6 EC Panorama course; it is not taken twice.
